part.text: The affected logic is centralized in `specs_setter::on_zero`: it correctly avoids numeric alignment when explicit alignment exists, but still overwrites the fill character with `0`. I’ll restrict that zero-fill assignment to the no-alignment case, preserving explicit alignment and fill behavior.

part.text:
Implemented the zero-flag precedence fix in `include/fmt/core.h`.

`on_zero()` now applies numeric alignment and zero fill only when no explicit alignment was specified. Thus `{:<06}` and `{:>06}` retain their alignment and use space padding, while `{:06}` still zero-pads.
